title: Tidewatch Backup Agent: Operations Runbook
key_sentences: This runbook describes how to install, configure and troubleshoot the Tidewatch backup agent on Linux servers.
It is written for the on-call engineers of the platform team.
Install the agent with the bootstrap script and check that the service has started.
The agent reads its settings from /etc/tidewatch/agent.yaml. A minimal file looks like this.
Snapshots are pruned after every successful run. To change the policy, follow these steps.
Every failed run writes one structured line to the journal. A typical entry is shown below.
If two consecutive runs fail with the same code, escalate in this order.
Questions about this runbook can be sent to the platform team mailbox.
Please include the agent version printed by the status command.

rows: Configuration file could not be parsed
Check network route and proxy settings
Fix permissions for the tidewatch user
Free space or raise the cache limit

list_items.text: A 64-bit Linux host with systemd 245 or later
At least 2 GB of free disk space for the local cache
Outbound HTTPS access to the backup endpoint
Edit the retention block in the configuration file.
Run tidewatch config check and read the output.
Confirm the new schedule with tidewatch status.
– Open an incident ticket and attach the last 200 journal lines.
– Inform the data owner if the gap exceeds 24 hours.

code:
$ curl -fsSL https://example.org/tidewatch/install.sh | sh
$ sudo systemctl enable --now tidewatch
$ tidewatch status

agent:
  name: edge-backup-01
  interval: 15m
targets:
  - path: /var/lib/app/data
    exclude: ["*.tmp", "cache/"]
retention:
  daily: 7
  weekly: 4
  monthly: 12
